title: Correlation measure for statistical systems
authors: V. I. Yukalov, E. P. Yukalova
abstract: A measure of correlations for statistical systems is advanced, called correlation index. The measure is general, being applicable to quantum and classical, equilibrium and nonequilibrium statistical systems. After formulating the general notion of correlation indices for arbitrary trace-class operators, the calculation of the correlation indices are illustrated by several examples of density operators and reduced density matrices. The computation of the correlation indices for equilibrium systems is exemplified for bosonic systems with the Bose-Einstein condensate, superconducting systems, and for spin systems. Correlation indices for nonequilibrium systems are considered for nonlinear dynamics of spin and pseudospin systems.
summary: This work introduces the correlation index, a general measure quantifying correlations in quantum and classical statistical systems. It applies this index to model complex phenomena in Bose-Einstein condensates, superconductors, and spin lattices. The resulting tool offers a powerful, unified diagnostic for studying correlation strength across equilibrium and non-equilibrium regimes.
main_problem: The paper develops a general, quantitative measure called the 'correlation index' ($\kappa$) to quantify the degree of correlations in diverse statistical systems.
main_result: The index successfully measures entanglement in quantum states and provides quantitative diagnostics for correlations in both equilibrium (e.g., BEC, superconductors) and non-equilibrium systems.
method: The index is defined using the ratio of operator norms: $\kappa(\hat{A}) \equiv \log  rac{||\hat{A}||}{||\hat{A}^{\otimes}||}$, applied to reduced density matrices ($\hat{ho}_2$) derived via partial tracing.
model_or_system: The theory is applied across multiple systems, including Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs), superconducting systems (BCS model), and general spin systems, covering both equilibrium and non-equilibrium dynamics.
key_observables: Correlation Index ($\kappa(\hat{A})$), Reduced Density Matrices ($\hat{ho}_2$), Von Neumann Entanglement Entropy ($S_E$), Condensate fraction ($n_0$).
important_parameters: Number of particles ($N$), Coupling parameter ($g$), Time ($t$), and the nature of the correlation (e.g., normal vs. anomalous averages in superconductors).
main_assumptions: Approximations include the Hartree-Fock-Bogolubov (HFB) approximation for superconductors and the use of partial traces to simplify density operators.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how $\kappa(\hat{ho}_2)$ changes with system size ($N$) or coupling strength ($g$) for BECs and superconductors, and how time-dependent correlations evolve in spin systems.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the general definition of the correlation index, then applies it to equilibrium systems like BECs and superconductors, and finally extends the analysis to non-equilibrium dynamics in spin and pseudospin systems.
why_interesting: The index provides a unified, mathematically rigorous diagnostic tool applicable across quantum many-body physics, linking concepts like entanglement entropy to measurable correlation strengths in systems ranging from superfluids to magnetic materials.
